preamble: Change of the palatal glide /j/ to the lateral approximant /l/. It is attested in two separate branches of Malayo-Polynesian. In the Central Papuan Oceanic language Motu, Proto-Oceanic *y between /a/ vowels appears as l (POc *puqaya 'crocodile' > huala, *maya 'tongue' > mala), though not in every environment (POc *kayu 'tree' > Motu au). In Sangir (Sangiric, northern Sulawesi), Proto-Austronesian *y likewise gives l: *buqaya 'crocodile' > buala, *daya 'upriver, toward the interior' > dala. No well-documented case outside Austronesian has been verified.

examples.note: Most Oceanic reflexes keep the glide or lose it (Dobuan, Roviana mea).
Most Philippine and western Indonesian languages keep the glide (Tagalog buáya, Malay buaya).

examples.to: dala e 'inland, toward the interior'; dala 'there behind, on the back side'
examples.note: Compare Saisiyat rayaʔ 'inland', with the glide kept.
